title: Acceptance probability at initialization
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let $T\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that every choice word of length exactly $T$ leads from the initial configuration of $N$ on $x$ to a halted configuration. Then the probability that a uniformly random length-$T$ choice word leads to a halted configuration whose output is exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$ equals the probability that the output after $T$ steps is exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$.
hypotheses_covered: N is a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine
Every length-T choice word halts from the initial configuration
